detail.title: Operational Foundations of Causal Memory (Revised)
detail.summary: This notebook synthesizes the criteria for causal memory, establishing that a persistent state only functions as memory when it provides predictive sufficiency or control utility relative to a specific coarse-grained model. Physical memory systems are bounded by the information-theoretic cost of maintaining these states against dissipation, with non-driven passive degrees of freedom modifying the effective entropy production rate.

detail.title: Synthesis of Operational Memory Foundations
detail.summary: This cycle completes the systematic revision of three core notebooks focusing on the thermodynamic and operational costs of memory. We integrate findings on coarse-graining, non-equilibrium driven dynamics, and passive degree-of-freedom coupling. Key insights identify that persistent physical states only function as effective memory when they demonstrably reduce future uncertainty or dissipation, a condition constrained by the resolution of the observer's model.
